- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.25) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25), model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is trending up.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1-2% above recent peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) for 5+ consecutive days, model shows persistent bias; apply mean reversion correction using 18-day rolling average.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overreacts to short-term sentiment shifts; use sentiment-weighted smoothing (e.g., 70% recent, 30% 18-day avg) to dampen volatility.
- If true outcome shows strong downward trend after forecast peak, model may have missed a correction; add 1-2 day lag correction to avoid premature peak.
